summary: Tested Change Password + Delete Account dashboard features and /trips routing. Backend: 8/8 pytest cases pass (wrong current pw, short pw 422, success + old pw fails + new pw works, auth required; delete wrong pw rejected, delete success decrements event attendees_count and inquiry/rsvp/user removed, only-admin blocked from deleting self; /trips travel-packages list+detail). Frontend: All critical UI flows pass (/trips lists seeded trip, /trips/:id shows detail, dashboard account-settings section + all 6 data-testids present, wrong current-pw -> 'incorrect' toast, mismatch -> 'match' toast, success -> 'Password updated' toast + form clears, re-login with new password works, delete wrong-pw -> 'incorrect' toast, delete success removes account and subsequent login returns 401, admin only-admin block with correct toast, Guidelines page 'My account' link to /dashboard present). Admin password restored (not changed).

integration_issues.issue: After successful account deletion the user is redirected to /auth instead of / (home). DeleteAccount.js calls logout() then navigate('/'), but RequireAuth on /dashboard likely intercepts the un-auth state and sends them to /auth before the navigate resolves. Spec said 'redirected to home'. Minor UX; toast still shows and deletion itself works.

action_items: Optional: in DeleteAccount.js, navigate('/') BEFORE calling logout(), or use navigate('/', { replace: true }) after a tick, so the user lands on home rather than /auth.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py delete_account loops through RSVPs with async-for and does one update_one per RSVP (N+1). For users with many RSVPs this is slow; consider aggregating event_id counts and doing bulk $inc operations.

server.py delete_account does not use a transaction, so a crash between the attendees_count decrements and users.delete_one could leave orphan state. Mongo sessions/transactions would make this atomic.

ChangePassword.js clears form on success but does not force re-authentication; existing JWT still valid for 30 days. Consider invalidating old sessions (bump a user token-version claim) on password change for better security.

DeleteAccount uses window.confirm() which is browser-default styling and not stylable; aligns with brutalist look but inconsistent with the sonner toast system; consider a shadcn AlertDialog for better UX.
test_credentials: Admin: admin@shenanigators.com / AdminPass123! (verified unchanged after tests). New TEST_* @example.com users created per test.
seed_data_creation: Several TEST_evt_*, TEST_trip_*, TEST_trip_route_*, TEST_FE_TripRoute_* records created and cleaned up by admin DELETE within tests. One extra TEST_FE_TripRoute_* trip from the frontend playwright run is NOT cleaned up (left behind for inspection).
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_account_mgmt.py covers full change-password + delete-account suite including only-admin guard. The admin only-admin test assumes admin@shenanigators.com is the sole admin — if another admin is promoted, that test will unexpectedly succeed deletion; be careful. Playwright flow registers a fresh TEST_fe_*@example.com user and deletes it in-flight so repeated runs are idempotent. Frontend lands user at /auth after deletion (minor nit).
rca of the issue: The /auth-after-delete behavior: logout() synchronously nulls the AuthContext user; React re-renders Dashboard, which is wrapped in RequireAuth; RequireAuth sees no user and <Navigate to="/auth"> replaces the pending navigate('/'). Fix: either (a) call navigate('/', { replace: true }) BEFORE logout() so the current route is no longer /dashboard when auth state flips, or (b) set a short setTimeout before logout.
